title: Storage
content: Engram stores all memory in a single embedded SQLite database with one writer. Chunks, facts, digests, and embeddings live in the same file; no separate server runs.

title: Temporal facts
content: Facts are stored with a validity interval. When a new fact contradicts an old one about the same entity and predicate, the old fact is superseded by setting its valid_until rather than deleting it, so history is preserved.

title: Hybrid recall
content: Recall fuses semantic vector similarity with lexical full-text BM25 using reciprocal rank fusion, then reranks by recency. Symbol-like queries weight the lexical signal higher.

title: Lazy eviction
content: Cold chunks are scored by age, time since last access, coverage, and access frequency. High-scoring chunks are moved out of the active database in batches. Frequently accessed content stays.

title: Year-sharded archive
content: Evicted chunks move into per-year archive database files. Sealed shards are opened read-only and searched newest first only when the user opts in, keeping the active set small and queries fast.

title: Document chunking
content: Markdown documents are split at heading boundaries of any level. Oversized sections are split at paragraph boundaries with overlap, never inside a fenced code block. Bare-heading and empty chunks are dropped.

title: Gitignore-aware indexing
content: The document indexer honors gitignore, ignore files, and the global gitignore, so files you already exclude from version control — secrets, build output — are never indexed into memory.

title: Static embeddings
content: Embeddings come from a static CPU model downloaded on first use and cached for offline reuse. Each embedding records its model identity so vectors from different models are never compared.

title: Consolidation ladder
content: Raw chunks roll up into session digests, then daily, weekly, and monthly digests, by aggregation only with no language model. Each level marks the level below as covered.

title: MCP server
content: Engram exposes recall, expand, and entity as tools over an MCP stdio server using line-delimited JSON-RPC, so a coding agent can query memory directly.

title: Loopback viewer
content: A blocking HTTP server bound to the loopback interface serves hook ingress and a human-readable viewer of recent chunks. It never binds to a public network interface.

title: Prune command
content: The prune command deletes indexed document chunks, or wipes all active memory entirely. Archive shards are left untouched by a prune.

title: Coverage tracking
content: When a chunk is summarized into a digest or distilled into a fact it is marked covered. Eviction favors covered, unaccessed chunks so that already-distilled content leaves the hot set first.

title: Out-of-band embedding
content: Capture commits a chunk synchronously and enqueues its embedding for an out-of-band worker, so write latency never depends on embedding computation.
